note: Display metadata for plant collections (cultivar/genus clusters). MEMBERSHIP lives on each plant.json as `collection:"<id>"`; this file only names the group, places it in a home section, picks the lead photo, and gives the blurb. See CLAUDE.md › Collections.

yarrows.name: Yarrows
yarrows.blurb: Achillea — flat-topped yarrows from the CO-native white species through the red, cerise, terracotta and pastel garden cultivars.

burnets.name: Burnets
burnets.blurb: Sanguisorba — bottlebrush burnets, from the xeric cucumber-leaved culinary herb to the moisture-loving maroon, pink and white border forms.

mulleins.name: Mulleins
mulleins.blurb: Verbascum — architectural flower-spire mulleins, the garden ornamentals (NOT the weedy common/moth mulleins).

apples.name: Apples
apples.blurb: Cold-hardy apple cultivars (Malus domestica) for the Front Range.

plums.name: Plums
plums.blurb: Hardy European, hybrid & native plums (Prunus) for our climate.

currants.name: Currants & gooseberries
currants.blurb: Ribes and their kin — currants, gooseberry, and the jostaberry hybrid.

pelargoniums.name: Pelargoniums
pelargoniums.blurb: Tender 'geraniums' (Pelargonium) — bedding, scented, ivy & regal types.

wallflowers.name: Wallflowers
wallflowers.blurb: Erysimum — fragrant cottage-garden wallflowers, perennial & biennial.

tulips.name: Tulips
tulips.blurb: Garden hybrid and perennializing species tulips.

crocuses.name: Crocuses
crocuses.blurb: Early snow crocus and big Dutch crocus for the first bees.

penstemons.name: Penstemons
penstemons.blurb: Beardtongues — Western native and garden penstemons.

maples.name: Maples
maples.blurb: Small Western maples (Acer) grown for fiery fall colour.

milkweeds.name: Milkweeds
milkweeds.blurb: Asclepias — the essential monarch host plants.

alliums.name: Alliums
alliums.blurb: Ornamental and wild onions (Allium) — globe and nodding flowerheads bees mob.

sunflowers.name: Sunflowers
sunflowers.blurb: True sunflowers (Helianthus) — golden heads bees and goldfinches mob.

bee-balms.name: Bee balms
bee-balms.blurb: Monarda — fragrant bergamots that draw bees & hummingbirds.

lupines.name: Lupines
lupines.blurb: Lupinus — native and garden pea-flower spires (toxic alkaloids).

dogwoods.name: Dogwoods
dogwoods.blurb: Cornus — winter stems, early flowers, and bird berries.

clematis.name: Clematis
clematis.blurb: Large-flowered garden climbers and native virgin's-bowers (Clematis).

columbines.name: Columbines
columbines.blurb: Aquilegia — spurred woodland-edge flowers, the wild blue and golden garden selections.

sweet-scabious.name: Scabious
sweet-scabious.blurb: Scabiosa — pincushion flowers: the compact perennial and the tall annual cut-flower forms.

prairie-coneflowers.name: Prairie coneflowers
prairie-coneflowers.blurb: Ratibida columnifera — the yellow Mexican hat and its mahogany-red form.

pinks.name: Pinks
pinks.blurb: Dianthus — fragrant, fringed, mat-forming garden pinks.

coreopsis.name: Coreopsis
coreopsis.blurb: Coreopsis — easy golden tickseed daisies, large-flowered and threadleaf.

sumacs.name: Sumacs
sumacs.blurb: Rhus — tough native shrubs for fiery fall color and tart red 'lemonade' berries.

primulas.name: Primulas
primulas.blurb: Primula — cool-season primroses: leaf rosettes topped with bright early flowers, from woodland classics to a Colorado alpine native.

ornamental-oregano.name: Ornamental oreganos
ornamental-oregano.blurb: Origanum — ornamental oreganos grown for their rosy flowers and cascading hop-like bracts (not the culinary herb).

marigolds.name: Marigolds
marigolds.blurb: Tagetes — cheerful, aromatic, deer-resistant marigolds, from tiny citrus-edible signets to big African pompoms and the tarragon-scented Mexican mint marigold.

bugleweeds.name: Bugleweeds
bugleweeds.blurb: Ajuga reptans — dark-leaved carpeting groundcovers with blue spring flower spikes for shade.

pasqueflowers.name: Pasqueflowers
pasqueflowers.blurb: Pulsatilla — furry-budded earliest-spring bells over ferny foliage, then feathery seedheads.

coral-bells.name: Coral bells
coral-bells.blurb: Heuchera — mounded semi-evergreen foliage under airy flower wands for dry shade.

elderberries.name: Elderberries
elderberries.blurb: Sambucus nigra selections — ornamental dark/cut-leaf forms and hardy fruiting elders; edible cooked flowers & berries.

poppies.name: Poppies
poppies.blurb: Papaver — crepe-paper poppies, from the huge oriental to the pastel Iceland.

peonies.name: Peonies
peonies.blurb: Paeonia — long-lived late-spring peonies, from the classic fragrant doubles to the fiery early singles.

hummingbird-mints.name: Hummingbird mints
hummingbird-mints.blurb: Agastache — aromatic xeric mints throwing spikes of tubular flowers hummingbirds work into fall.

four-oclocks.name: Four o'clocks
four-oclocks.blurb: Mirabilis — the native desert four o'clock and the old-fashioned garden annual, both opening on late-afternoon air.

evening-primroses.name: Evening primroses
evening-primroses.blurb: Oenothera — low xeric mats of big silky day- or evening-opening cups.

oregon-grapes.name: Oregon grapes
oregon-grapes.blurb: Berberis — holly-leaved evergreens with golden spring flowers and blue berries, in a low native mat and an upright screen.

lindens.name: Lindens
lindens.blurb: Tilia — big heart-leaved shade trees whose fragrant summer flowers are among the best bee forage there is.

hawthorns.name: Hawthorns
hawthorns.blurb: Crataegus — thorny small trees with white spring flower clusters and red haws that feed birds all winter.

rhododendrons.name: Rhododendrons & azaleas
rhododendrons.blurb: The hardiest Rhododendron for the Front Range — evergreen rhodo and deciduous azalea, both needing an acid-mix bed away from our alkaline clay.

phloxes.name: Phloxes
phloxes.blurb: Phlox — sweetly fragrant clustered flowers, from the tall summer border spires to the low spring woodland haze.

sages.name: Sages
sages.blurb: Ornamental Salvia — aromatic, deer-proof mounds throwing wands of tubular flowers bees and hummingbirds work all season.

honeysuckle-vines.name: Honeysuckle vines
honeysuckle-vines.blurb: Twining Lonicera — cold-hardy climbers hung with long scarlet-to-coral tubes hummingbirds work all summer.

speedwells.name: Speedwells
speedwells.blurb: Veronica — starry blue-to-white flowers, on upright border candlesticks and flat evergreen creeping mats.

lambs-ears.name: Lamb's ears
lambs-ears.blurb: Stachys byzantina — the woolly silver mat, from the flowering species to the big-leaved and flowerless garden selections.
